mainTopic: Judgment of the בינונים and of sinners in גיהנם, how God tilts the scale toward kindness, and forgiveness for one who forgives others
overview: This amud continues a ברייתא about the final Day of Judgment. It opens with בית שמאי's view that the בינונים (people whose merits and sins are balanced) go down to גיהנם, cry out, and come back up. בית הלל disagree and say that God, who is 'רב חסד', tilts the scale toward kindness and saves them. The ברייתא then describes the punishment of sinners. 'פושעי ישראל בגופן' and gentile sinners are judged for twelve months and then destroyed. The gravest sinners, such as מינין, מסורות, אפיקורסים, and those who led the masses to sin, are punished even beyond the end of גיהנם. The גמרא then answers a challenge to בית הלל from זכריה's 'third part through the fire': that פסוק is about balanced people who also sinned with their bodies. רב defines that body-sin as never wearing תפילין, and רב חסדא explains who 'spread terror in the land of the living' is: a leader who rules by too much fear. The גמרא then explains how God tilts the scale. רבי אליעזר says He presses down, רבי יוסי בר חנינא says He lifts the sins, and the school of רבי ישמעאל says He sets aside each first sin. רבא teaches that whoever lets go of what others owe him is forgiven by Heaven, and the story of רב הונא's recovery illustrates this. The amud ends as רבי אחא בר חנינא begins to explain 'לשארית נחלתו', a teaching that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The middle group goes down, cries out, and comes back up
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי finish their description of the בינונים: they go down to גיהנם, cry out in pain, and then rise up. The proof is a פסוק in זכריה about refining 'the third part' in fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...and they cry out and come up, as it says: 'And I will bring the third part through the fire, and refine them as silver is refined, and test them as gold is tested. They will call in My name, and I will answer them.'
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of בית שמאי's statement about the בינונים, the people who are neither fully righteous nor fully wicked. בית שמאי say these people go down to גיהנם briefly, cry out, and are then brought back up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, the בינונים are not lost forever. Their time in גיהנם works like a refining process that cleans them. The פסוק in זכריה speaks of 'the third' group, meaning the third of the three groups. That group is put through fire like silver and gold, and then 'calls in My name' and is answered. This shows they come out purified.

keyTerms.meaning: The middle group, people whose merits and sins are balanced (the subject of this passage)
They cry out or chirp, meaning they wail in pain
And they come up (out of גיהנם)
The third part, read here as the third group
And I will refine them (like metal in a furnace)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud opens mid-sentence. The words 'they cry out and come up' are about the בינונים according to בית שמאי. They are not about the completely wicked.

phrases.english: and they cry out and come up,
phrases.notes: Continues בית שמאי's description of the בינונים going down to גיהנם

phrases.english: as it says: 'And I will bring the third part through the fire,'
and I will refine them as silver is refined,
and I will test them as gold is tested;

phrases.aramaic: הוּא יִקְרָא בִשְׁמִי וַאֲנִי אֶעֱנֶה אוֹתוֹ״,
phrases.english: he will call in My name and I will answer him.'
phrases.notes: They cry out (מצפצפין) and are answered, so they come up (עולין)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues בית שמאי's opinion in the ברייתא from the previous section about the three groups
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, the בינונים go down to גיהנם, cry out, and are brought back up, as the פסוק describes refining 'the third' in fire.

steps.title: חנה's prayer describes the middle group
steps.stepSummary: A second פסוק, from חנה's prayer, is applied to the בינונים: God brings down to שאול and brings up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about them חנה said: 'God kills and gives life; He brings down to the grave and brings up.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds another פסוק to support בית שמאי's view. חנה's words 'He brings down to שאול and brings up' describe the בינונים exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק showed that the בינונים are refined. This פסוק shows the full path: down into the grave (גיהנם) and then back up. It strengthens the picture of a temporary descent rather than a permanent one.

keyTerms.meaning: And about them, a formula linking a פסוק to a particular group
He brings down to the grave (the underworld)

phrases.english: And about them Hannah said:
'The Lord kills and gives life;'
He brings down to the grave and brings up.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק supporting the same claim about the בינונים
steps.raayaObject: בית שמאי's claim that the בינונים go down to גיהנם and come back up

steps.title: בית הלל: God tilts the scale toward kindness
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל disagree with בית שמאי. Because God is 'רב חסד', He tilts the balanced scale toward kindness, so the בינונים are spared from גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say: 'And abundant in kindness' means He tilts the scale toward kindness.
steps.whatsHappening: Now בית הלל give their opinion about the בינונים. They say God does not send them to גיהנם at all, because He leans toward mercy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בינונים have an exactly balanced scale. בית שמאי said they must be refined in גיהנם. בית הלל read 'ורב חסד' from the י״ג מדות as teaching that God tips a balanced scale toward the side of merit. So the בינונים are spared.

keyTerms.meaning: And abundant in kindness, one of God's thirteen attributes of mercy

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core disagreement between בית שמאי and בית הלל about the בינונים: refinement through suffering versus being saved by God's kindness.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel say:
'And abundant in kindness' (שמות 34:6) — He tilts toward kindness.
phrases.notes: God tips the balanced scale to the side of merit

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to בית שמאי on the fate of the בינונים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית הלל, God tilts the balanced scale of the בינונים toward kindness, so they are spared from גיהנם.

steps.title: דוד's words in הלל describe the middle group
steps.stepSummary: Two lines from תהלים 116 are applied to the בינונים according to בית הלל: 'I love that God hears my voice' and 'I was brought low, and He saved me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And about them דוד said: 'I love that God hears my voice.' And about them דוד said the whole passage: 'I was brought low, and He saved me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings פסוקים to support בית הלל's view. דוד המלך's words in תהלים are read as describing the בינונים, whom God saves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'דלותי' (I was brought low) is read as 'I was poor,' meaning poor in מצוות. Even so, 'ולי יהושיע': God saves him. This matches בית הלל exactly. The בינונים lack merits, yet God's kindness rescues them.

keyTerms.meaning: The entire passage (the whole chapter applies to them)
I was brought low or poor, read as poor in מצוות

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי: the בינונים go down to גיהנם, are refined, and come up (זכריה, חנה). בית הלל: God tilts toward kindness and saves them (תהלים 116).

phrases.english: And about them David said:
'I love that the Lord hears my voice' (תהלים 116:1),

phrases.aramaic: וַעֲלֵיהֶם אָמַר דָּוִד כׇּל הַפָּרָשָׁה כּוּלָּהּ —
phrases.english: and about them David said the entire passage:
'I was brought low, and He saved me' (תהלים 116:6).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports בית הלל's view with פסוקים
steps.raayaObject: בית הלל's claim that God saves the בינונים through kindness

steps.title: Sinners with their bodies are judged twelve months, then destroyed
steps.stepSummary: Jewish sinners 'בגופן' and gentile sinners 'בגופן' are judged in גיהנם for twelve months. Afterward their bodies and souls are destroyed and become ashes under the feet of the צדיקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Jewish sinners who sinned with their bodies, and gentile sinners who sinned with their bodies, go down to גיהנם and are judged there for twelve months. After twelve months, their body is consumed, their soul is burned, and a wind scatters them under the soles of the feet of the righteous, as it says: 'You will trample the wicked, for they will be ashes under the soles of your feet.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now moves on from the בינונים to describe the punishment of a category of real sinners. These sinners suffer for twelve months and then cease to exist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a limited punishment: twelve months of judgment, followed by complete destruction rather than endless suffering. The פסוק in מלאכי, 'they will be ashes under your feet', is the source for their ending as ashes. What exactly 'sinning with the body' means is explained later by the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Jewish sinners who sinned with their bodies (the גמרא defines this later)
גיהנם, the place of punishment after death

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this group up with the בינונים. The בינונים (according to בית שמאי) come back up. This group does not come back up. They are destroyed after twelve months.

phrases.english: Jewish sinners with their bodies,
and sinners of the nations of the world with their bodies —
go down to Gehenna
and are judged there for twelve months.
After twelve months —
their body is consumed, and their soul is burned,
and a wind scatters them
under the soles of the feet of the righteous,
as it says: 'And you shall trample the wicked,'
for they will be ashes
under the soles of your feet.'

steps.triggerLanguage: פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּגוּפָן, וּפוֹשְׁעֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם בְּגוּפָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the בינונים to the punishment of sinners
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Jewish and gentile sinners 'בגופן' are judged in גיהנם for twelve months and then destroyed, becoming ashes under the feet of the צדיקים.

steps.title: The most severe sinners are judged for endless generations
steps.stepSummary: A list of the gravest sinners (מינין, מסורות, אפיקורסים, deniers of the תורה and of תחיית המתים, those who separated from the community, those who spread terror, and those who caused the masses to sin like ירבעם) are judged in גיהנם for generations upon generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the heretics, the informers, and the אפיקורסים; those who denied the תורה; those who denied תחיית המתים; those who separated from the ways of the community; those who spread their terror in the land of the living; and those who sinned and caused the many to sin, like ירבעם בן נבט and his companions: they go down to גיהנם and are judged there for generations upon generations, as it says: 'And they will go out and look at the corpses of the men who rebelled against Me...'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא contrasts the previous group with a much worse group of sinners. These do not get off after twelve months; their punishment lasts for generations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אבל' (but) marks the contrast with the twelve-month group. What these sinners have in common is that their sins attack the foundations of the faith or harm the whole community, not just personal wrongdoing. The פסוק in ישעיה, which continues 'their worm will not die and their fire will not be quenched', is the source for a punishment that does not end.

keyTerms.meaning: Informers who hand Jews over to the authorities
Those who scorn the תורה and its scholars
Their terror or fear (that they imposed on others)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two levels of sinners: (1) 'פושעים בגופן', twelve months and then destroyed; (2) heretics, informers, deniers, and those who mislead the masses, judged for endless generations.
steps.whyThisMatters: This list defines which sins are so destructive that they put a person outside the normal limited punishment. It parallels similar lists in סנהדרין of those with no share in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: But the heretics and the informers
and the apostates (apikorsim),
those who denied the Torah,
and those who denied the resurrection of the dead,
and those who separated from the ways of the community,
phrases.notes: They did not share in the community's troubles

phrases.english: and those who spread their terror in the land of the living,
and those who sinned and caused the masses to sin,
such as Jeroboam son of Nebat and his companions —
go down to Gehenna
and are judged there for generations upon generations,
as it says: 'And they will go out and look'
at the corpses of the men who rebelled against Me, etc.'
phrases.notes: The verse continues: their worm will not die and their fire will not be quenched

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with the twelve-month punishment of step 5 by presenting a far more severe category
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heretics, informers, אפיקורסים, deniers of the תורה and of תחיית המתים, those who separate from the community, those who spread terror, and those who lead the masses to sin are judged in גיהנם for endless generations.

steps.title: Their punishment outlasts גיהנם itself
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues about the gravest sinners. גיהנם will come to an end, but their punishment will not.
steps.simpleTranslation: גיהנם will end, but they will not end. As it says: 'Their form will wear out שאול, from His dwelling.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps describing the worst sinners from the last step. It adds that their punishment lasts even longer than גיהנם itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said they are judged 'for generations upon generations.' Now the ברייתא goes further: גיהנם wears out before they do. The פסוק is read as 'their form outlasts שאול.'

keyTerms.meaning: comes to an end, is used up

phrases.english: Gehinnom comes to an end, but they do not come to an end,
as it is said: "And their form shall wear out the netherworld
from His dwelling"
phrases.notes: This word זבול will be explained in the next step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the description of the gravest sinners from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The worst sinners' punishment lasts beyond the end of גיהנם itself.

steps.title: Why so harsh: they attacked the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that the reason for this severe punishment is that they 'stretched out their hands' against the זבול, which means the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why all this? Because they stretched out their hands against the זבול, as it says 'from His dwelling (זבול).' And זבול means only the בית המקדש, as it says: 'I have surely built You a house of זבול.' About them חנה said: 'God's enemies will be shattered.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks why these sinners deserve such a harsh punishment. It answers that they harmed the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זבול in the earlier פסוק is the key. A second פסוק, from שלמה's prayer, shows that זבול means the בית המקדש. So the same פסוק that describes the punishment also hints at its cause. חנה's words are then applied to these people.

keyTerms.meaning: they stretched out their hands, meaning they attacked or damaged
dwelling, here meaning the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And why all this?
Because they stretched out their hands against the 'zevul,'
as it is said: "from His dwelling (zevul)",
and 'zevul' means nothing other than the Temple,
as it is said: "I have surely built You a house of dwelling (zevul)",
and about them Hannah said:
"The adversaries of the Lord shall be shattered."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the punishment described in step 7, using the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extreme punishment comes because they attacked the בית המקדש, which is called זבול.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא ends with three groups. Most צדיקים and רשעים have clear outcomes. The בינונים are debated by בית שמאי and בית הלל. The very worst sinners, those who attacked the בית המקדש, are punished even beyond גיהנם.

steps.title: Their faces are like the bottom of a pot
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבין adds that the faces of these sinners will be black like the bottom of a pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר אבין said: Their faces will look like the bottom of a pot.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא adds a short picture of what these sinners will look like on the Day of Judgment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing legal changes here. It is an aggadic addition: their faces will be dark and sooty, like a pot that has sat on the fire, showing their shame.

keyTerms.meaning: the bottom of a pot, which is blackened by fire

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avin said:
And their faces are like the bottom of a pot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An אמורא's comment on the sinners described in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The faces of these sinners will be blackened like the bottom of a pot.

steps.title: רבא: even the finest of מחוזא are among them
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even the most 'beautiful' (most pampered and well-off) people of מחוזא will be called people of גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And they include the most beautiful of the people of מחוזא, and they will be called 'people of גיהנם.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a sharp comment about his own region. Even the finest-looking people of מחוזא will be counted among the people of גיהנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מחוזא was a wealthy town known for pampered living. רבא is warning that outward beauty and status do not protect a person. People who look the best can still be called 'בני גיהנם.'

keyTerms.meaning: a wealthy town in בבל where רבא lived
people of גיהנם, those who belong there

phrases.english: And Rava said:
And they include the most beautiful of the people of Mechoza,
and they are called "people of Gehinnom."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second אמורא's comment, adding to step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the finest-looking people of מחוזא can be counted as בני גיהנם.

steps.title: Challenge to בית הלל from 'the third part through the fire'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to בית הלל's rule that God tilts toward kindness. It asks: doesn't a פסוק say that a third group is brought through fire?
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said: בית הלל say 'and abundant in kindness' means He tilts toward kindness. But it is written: 'I will bring the third part through the fire!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to בית הלל's view from step 3 and challenges it with a פסוק in זכריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל said the בינונים are spared from גיהנם. But זכריה speaks of a 'third' group that goes through fire and is then purified. That sounds exactly like בינונים going briefly to גיהנם, which seems to fit בית שמאי instead.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the master said,' the formula for going back to discuss an earlier quote
but isn't it written? (introduces a challenge from a פסוק)
the third part, a third group

steps.confusionAlert: 'אמר מר' does not start a new teaching. It only re-quotes a line from earlier in the ברייתא (step 3) so the גמרא can analyze it.

phrases.english: The master said: Beit Hillel say:
"And abundant in kindness" means He tilts toward kindness.
But it is written: "And I will bring the third part through the fire"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadic comments and returns to בית הלל's view from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's claim that the בינונים do not go to גיהנם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: זכריה describes a 'third' group sent through fire for purification, which sounds like בינונים being sent to גיהנם.

steps.title: That פסוק is about those who sinned with their bodies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that זכריה's 'third part' refers to Jewish sinners who sinned with their bodies, not to ordinary בינונים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about Jewish sinners who sinned with their bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends בית הלל by saying the 'third part through fire' is a different group of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'third part' is not the ordinary בינוני. It refers to פושעי ישראל בגופן, who were mentioned in step 5. So בית הלל's rule for regular בינונים still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Jewish sinners who sinned with their bodies (for example, a person who never put on תפילין)

phrases.english: There, it refers to Jewish sinners who sinned with their bodies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11 by saying the פסוק is about a different group.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the פסוק to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'third part' means ordinary בינונים, which would contradict בית הלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'third part' means פושעי ישראל בגופן, so בית הלל's rule for regular בינונים is unaffected.

steps.title: But those sinners were said to have no fix
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges its own answer. Step 5 said that sinners with their bodies are destroyed after twelve months. So how can they be the 'third part' that is purified?
steps.simpleTranslation: Jewish sinners with their bodies? But you said they have no fix!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave by pointing to what was said earlier about these same sinners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said פושעי ישראל בגופן are judged for twelve months and then turned to ash. That means they have no repair. But זכריה's 'third part' is refined and comes out pure. So the two do not seem to match.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't you say? (points to a contradiction with an earlier statement)
they have no fix or repair

phrases.english: Jewish sinners who sinned with their bodies?
But didn't you say they have no fix?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that זכריה's 'third part' refers to פושעי ישראל בגופן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא said these sinners are destroyed and have no fix. The 'third part,' however, is purified and saved.

steps.title: No fix only when most deeds are sins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the difference. Sinners with their bodies have no fix only when most of their deeds are sins. The 'third part' is about people who are half and half, but who also have that body-sin. They must pass through the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: When do they have no fix? When most of their deeds are sins. Here, it is half sins and half merits, and among the sins is also the sin of sinning with the body. Such a person cannot avoid 'I will bring the third part through the fire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting the sinners-with-their-bodies into two cases, depending on how many sins they have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If most of a person's deeds are sins and he sinned with his body, he is destroyed. If he is exactly half and half, but his sins include sinning with the body, he does not get the kindness 'tilt.' He goes briefly through the fire and is purified. Both statements are true, because each describes a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: most of a person's deeds are sins
half sins and half merits, a בינוני
he cannot avoid, it must be that

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לֵית לְהוּ תַּקָּנָה — בְּרוֹב עֲוֹנוֹת.
phrases.english: When do they have no fix? When the majority of their deeds are sins.
Here, it is half sins and half merits,
and among them there is also the sin
of Jewish sinners who sinned with their bodies;
it is not possible for him to avoid
"And I will bring the third part through the fire."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי לֵית לְהוּ תַּקָּנָה — בְּרוֹב עֲוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 by dividing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All sinners with their bodies have no fix, so they cannot be the purified 'third part.'
steps.terutzMaskana: Only those with most deeds as sins have no fix. Half-and-half people with a body-sin go through the fire and are purified.

steps.title: Without that sin, the balanced person is saved by kindness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that a half-and-half person without the body-sin gets God's kindness tilt, which keeps בית הלל's view. דוד's words 'I love that God hears' refer to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if not (if they lack that sin), 'abundant in kindness' means He tilts toward kindness. About them דוד said: 'I love that God hears.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer and confirms בית הלל's rule for ordinary בינונים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full picture is now clear. A half-and-half person who did not sin with his body is spared from גיהנם through 'רב חסד.' A half-and-half person with that sin passes briefly through the fire. A person with mostly sins plus that sin is destroyed. דוד's פסוק from step 4 is again tied to the saved בינונים.

keyTerms.meaning: and if not (if this condition is missing)

steps.whatToRemember: Three cases: (1) half and half, no body-sin: God tilts toward kindness, and the person is saved (בית הלל). (2) Half and half with a body-sin: 'the third part through the fire,' meaning brief purification. (3) Mostly sins with a body-sin: no fix.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא settles an apparent contradiction between a פסוק and a ruling. Instead of rejecting either one, it defines exactly which person each source is talking about.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו, ״וְרַב חֶסֶד״ — מַטֶּה כְּלַפֵּי חֶסֶד.
phrases.english: But if not, "and abundant in kindness" means He tilts toward kindness.
And about them David said:
"I love that the Lord hears."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם לָאו, וְרַב חֶסֶד מַטֶּה כְּלַפֵּי חֶסֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of step 14 and confirms בית הלל's rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בית הלל's 'רב חסד' applies to half-and-half people who did not sin with their bodies. זכריה's 'third part through the fire' applies to half-and-half people who did.

steps.title: רבא explains why the Jewish people feel loved by God
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the פסוק 'אהבתי כי ישמע ה׳'. The Jewish people feel loved when God hears their prayers. Even though they are 'poor' in מצוות, it is fitting for God to save them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: What does the פסוק 'I love that God hears' mean? The Jewish people said to God: 'Master of the world, when do I know You love me? When You listen to my prayers.' The next פסוק says 'I was poor, and He saved me.' This means: even though I am poor in מצוות, it is right for You to save me.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 15 said that דוד's words 'אהבתי כי ישמע ה׳' refer to the בינונים. Now רבא explains what that פסוק means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the פסוק as the voice of כנסת ישראל speaking to God. The proof of God's love is that He answers prayers even when we are 'poor' in מצוות. This fits the idea of the בינוני, whose merits are not enough on their own but who is still saved by God's kindness.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught / explained a פסוק in a deeper (homiletic) way
The Jewish people as one whole nation

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives an emotional picture of what 'tilting toward kindness' means. God saves us even when our record of מצוות is thin.

phrases.english: Rava taught: What is the meaning of what is written:
"I love that God hears" —

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: The Jewish people said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:

phrases.aramaic: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, אֵימָתַי אֲנִי אֲהוּבָה לְפָנֶיךָ —
phrases.english: Master of the world, when am I loved before You?
When You hear the sound of my prayers.
"I was poor, and He saved me" —

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁדַּלָּה אֲנִי מִן הַמִּצְוֹת —
phrases.english: even though I am poor in מצוות —
it is fitting to save me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the פסוק that step 15 applied to the בינונים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God's love is shown by answering prayers. It is fitting for Him to save us even when we are poor in מצוות.

steps.title: Who are the Jewish sinners with their bodies?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא from step 5. It asks what the term 'פושעי ישראל בגופן' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The 'Jewish sinners with their bodies,' who are they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a phrase from the earlier ברייתא and asks what kind of person it describes. This sets up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 12-14 depended on this group, but the term was never explained. Now the גמרא wants a clear definition of 'sinning with the body.'

keyTerms.meaning: Jewish sinners who sin with their body
What is it? / Who are they?

phrases.english: The Jewish sinners with their bodies,
who are they?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of רבא's teaching and goes back to define a term from the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A definition of the phrase 'פושעי ישראל בגופן'.

steps.title: רב: a head that never wore תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that a Jewish sinner with his body is someone whose head never wore תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It is the skull that never put on תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב defines the term from step 17. A 'body-sinner' is a person who never put תפילין on his head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sin is called 'with the body' because the מצוה of תפילין is done on the body itself. Never doing it at all shows a total rejection of that bodily מצוה.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not someone who skipped תפילין once. It describes a head that never put on תפילין at all.

phrases.english: Rav said:
A skull that did not put on תפילין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Jewish body-sinners are people who never put on תפילין.

steps.title: רב: non-Jewish body-sinners are those who commit sexual sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about the non-Jewish body-sinners. רב answers: those who commit 'the sin' (forbidden relations).
steps.simpleTranslation: The sinners of the nations with their bodies, who are they? רב said: Those who commit 'the sin.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question about non-Jews, and רב answers right away. The question is short and only hinted at.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For non-Jews, the 'body sin' is a sin done with the body itself, meaning forbidden relations (עריות). So a different sin defines the same term for each group.

phrases.english: The sinners of the nations of the world with their bodies —
Rav said: with 'the sin' (forbidden relations).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same kind of question as step 17, now about non-Jews, and answers it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Non-Jewish body-sinners are those who commit forbidden relations.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the leader who rules by fear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defines another phrase from the ברייתא: 'those who cast their fear over the land of the living.' רב חסדא says this is a פרנס who scares the community too much, and not for the sake of Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And those who cast their fear over the land of the living' — רב חסדא said: This is a community leader who puts too much fear on the community, and not for the sake of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defines one more group from the ברייתא's list of the gravest sinners in step 6. רב חסדא explains who they are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא listed people who are punished forever, and this group sounded unclear. רב חסדא says it is a harsh leader who uses too much fear for his own power or honor, not to serve God.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for the sake of Heaven

steps.confusionAlert: A leader is allowed to have authority. The problem is only fear that is too much and not for the sake of Heaven.

phrases.english: And those who cast their fear over the land of the living —
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא, based on יחזקאל 32

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה פַּרְנָס הַמַּטִּיל אֵימָה יְתֵירָה עַל הַצִּבּוּר
phrases.english: This is a leader who puts too much fear on the community
not for the sake of Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues defining terms from the ברייתא, moving to the next group in the list.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a פרנס who frightens the community too much, not for the sake of Heaven.

steps.title: A harsh leader will not have a scholar for a son
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, adds a punishment: such a פרנס will not have a son who is a תלמיד חכם. He brings a פסוק from איוב as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Any leader who puts too much fear on the community, not for the sake of Heaven, will not see a son who is a תלמיד חכם. The פסוק says: 'So people fear him; he will not see any wise-hearted ones.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the harsh leader was just mentioned, the גמרא adds a related teaching about his punishment in this world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links two things: 'people fear him' and 'he will not see the wise-hearted.' רב reads this as a measure-for-measure punishment. The one who made others afraid of him loses wise children.
steps.whyThisMatters: It is a practical warning about how leaders should treat their community.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל פַּרְנָס הַמַּטִּיל אֵימָה יְתֵירָה עַל הַצִּבּוּר
phrases.english: Any leader who puts too much fear on the community
not for the sake of Heaven
will not see a son who is a Torah scholar,
as it says: "Therefore people fear him;
he will not see any of the wise-hearted."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related teaching about the same harsh פרנס defined in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פרנס who rules with too much fear, not for the sake of Heaven, will not have a son who is a תלמיד חכם.

steps.title: Back to בית הלל: God tilts toward kindness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes בית הלל's line from the ברייתא again: God, who is 'abundant in kindness,' tilts the scale toward kindness. This sets up a question about how that works.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say: God is 'abundant in kindness,' so He tilts the scale toward kindness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back בית הלל's words from the ברייתא. It is setting up the next question: how exactly does God tilt the scale?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 11-15 showed that this rule applies to the בינוני. Now the גמרא repeats it for a new purpose: to explain how the tilting actually works.

keyTerms.meaning: And abundant in kindness (from the י״ג מדות)

phrases.english: Beit Hillel say: "And abundant in kindness" —
He tilts toward kindness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the definitions and returns to בית הלל's rule, quoting it again for a new question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God tilts the judgment of the בינוני toward kindness.

steps.title: How does God tilt the scale?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how God actually tilts the scale toward kindness.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does He do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the method behind בית הלל's rule. This sets up two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בינוני's merits and sins are equal. The question is what God does to the scale to make it come out good.

phrases.english: How does He do it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the rule quoted in step 22 works.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How God tips the balanced scale toward merit.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: God presses down the merits
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says God 'presses down' (כובשו), tipping the scale toward merit. His source is the פסוק 'He will again have mercy on us; He will press down our sins.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: He presses it down. As it says: 'He will again have mercy on us; He will press down our sins.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first answer to 'how does God tilt the scale?' רבי אליעזר says God presses down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture a balance scale. Following the Sefaria explanation, God pushes down the side of the merits so they outweigh the sins. The proof is the word יכבוש in מיכה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: He presses it down,
as it says: "He will again have mercy on us;
He will press down our sins."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: God presses down the scale toward merit (כובשו).

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר חנינא: God lifts up the sins
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא says God 'lifts' (נושא) the side of the sins, so they weigh less. His source is 'He lifts sin and passes over transgression.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: He lifts. As it says: 'He lifts sin and passes over transgression.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second answer to the same question. Instead of pressing the merits down, God lifts the sins up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers end the same way: the scale tips toward merit. They differ only in which side God acts on. רבי יוסי בר חנינא reads נושא עון as lifting the sins off the scale.

keyTerms.meaning: Lifts / carries (raises the side of the sins)

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל: God tilts the בינוני's judgment toward kindness. רבי אליעזר says He presses the merits down (כובשו). רבי יוסי בר חנינא says He lifts the sins up (נושא). Either way, the result is the same.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר: נוֹשֵׂא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said: He lifts,
as it says: "He lifts sin and passes over transgression."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר: נוֹשֵׂא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different method from רבי אליעזר's answer in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: God lifts the side of the sins (נושא), so the merits outweigh them.

steps.title: God sets aside each first sin
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל gives a third explanation of how God tilts the scale. He removes each first sin from the count.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Sage of the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: He passes over each first sin, and that is His way of kindness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third answer to the question of how God tilts the scale toward kindness. This answer comes from a ברייתא of the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said God presses down the merits, and רבי יוסי בר חנינא said He lifts the sins. This ברייתא says something different: God takes the first sin off the scale. With one sin removed, a person who was evenly balanced now has more merits than sins.

keyTerms.meaning: A Sage of the school of רבי ישמעאל taught (introduces a ברייתא)
Attribute, way of acting (here, God's attribute of mercy)

phrases.english: A Sage of the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
He passes over each first [sin],
phrases.notes: God sets the first sin aside so it does not count on the scale.

phrases.english: and that is the attribute [of mercy].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third answer to the question in step 23, alongside רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי בר חנינא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does God tilt the scale toward kindness?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: God passes over each first sin, removing it from the count.

steps.title: The set-aside sin is not erased
steps.stepSummary: רבא clarifies that the first sin is only set aside, not deleted. If a person's sins are the majority, it is counted again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: But the sin itself is not erased. If the person has mostly sins, that sin is counted together with them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to the ברייתא. The first sin is only set aside to help a person who is close to the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kindness of removing the first sin only matters when it can tip the balance toward merit. If the person has more sins than merits anyway, the 'removed' sin goes back into the count and he is judged for all of them. So the sin is only on hold. It is not deleted.

keyTerms.meaning: It is counted together with them

phrases.english: Rava said:
But the sin itself is not erased.
For if there is a majority of sins,
it is counted together with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וְעָוֹן עַצְמוֹ אֵינוֹ נִמְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on the ברייתא of דבי רבי ישמעאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first sin is only set aside to tip a balanced person toward merit. If sins are the majority, it is counted again.

steps.title: One who lets things go is forgiven
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads 'נושא עון ועובר על פשע' as a promise. God forgives the sins of a person who lets go of what others owe him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Whoever lets go of what others owe him, Heaven lets go of all his sins. The פסוק says, 'He bears sin and passes over transgression.' Whose sin does He bear? The sin of the one who passes over transgression done against him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new reading of the פסוק that רבי יוסי בר חנינא used. In רבא's reading, the פסוק tells us whose sins God forgives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the two halves of the פסוק as cause and result. God 'bears sin' for the person who 'passes over transgression,' meaning one who does not insist on getting back at people who wronged him. God treats a person the way that person treats others.

keyTerms.meaning: One who lets go of his reckonings (does not hold others to account)

steps.confusionAlert: Here מדותיו does NOT mean 'character traits.' It means one's reckonings or claims against others. מעביר על מדותיו means letting go of what people owe you or did to you.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source that being forgiving toward others earns forgiveness from Heaven. It sets up the story that follows.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Whoever lets go of his reckonings [with others],
they pass over all his transgressions for him,
as it is stated: “He bears sin and passes over transgression.”
For whom does He bear sin?
For one who passes over transgression [done to him].

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: כׇּל הַמַּעֲבִיר עַל מִדּוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different reading of the same פסוק that רבי יוסי בר חנינא used in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever lets go of what others owe him has all his sins let go by Heaven.

steps.title: רב הונא nearly dies and recovers
steps.stepSummary: A story: רב פפא visits the very sick רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע and tells people to prepare his shrouds. רב הונא recovers, and רב פפא is embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע became ill, and רב פפא went in to visit him. He saw that he was dying and said to those there: Prepare his provisions (shrouds). In the end he recovered, and רב פפא was embarrassed to see him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that will illustrate רבא's teaching. This step sets the scene for the question and answer that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא was sure רב הונא would die, but he survived. That raises the obvious question of what saved him. The answer comes in step 31.

keyTerms.meaning: To ask about his welfare (visit the sick)
Provisions for a journey; here, burial shrouds

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ חֲלַשׁ,
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, became ill;
Rav Pappa went in to ask about his welfare.
He saw that the world was growing weak for him (he was dying),
he said to them: Prepare provisions (shrouds) for him.
In the end he recovered,
and Rav Pappa was embarrassed to see him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ חֲלַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that will support רבא's teaching in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא was close to death but recovered unexpectedly.

steps.title: What did you see?
steps.stepSummary: People ask רב הונא what he saw while he was near death.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: What did you see?
steps.whatsHappening: People ask רב הונא what happened while he hung between life and death. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question asks for the hidden reason behind his recovery. His answer will tie the story directly back to the פסוק רבא used.

phrases.english: They said to him: What did you see?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the recovery described in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What happened in Heaven while רב הונא was near death?

steps.title: Saved because he let things go
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says he really was about to die. But God told the heavenly court not to be strict with him, because he was never strict with others.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Yes, it was so. But the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them: Since he does not insist on his rights, do not insist with him. As it says, 'He bears sin and passes over transgression.' For whom does He bear sin? For one who passes over transgression.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא explains that he was saved because he always let go of what others owed him. God judged him the same gentle way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא had been right that רב הונא was dying. The judgment changed because of רב הונא's forgiving nature. The story uses the same פסוק and the same reading as רבא, so it serves as a real-life proof of רבא's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not stand on his rights or insist on his claims
Do not be exacting with him

steps.whatToRemember: How you treat others is how Heaven treats you. If you are not strict with people who wrong you, Heaven will not be strict with you, as רבא teaches and the story of רב הונא shows.

phrases.english: He said to them: Yes, it was so [I was dying],
but the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them (the heavenly court):
Since he does not stand on his rights,
do not be exacting with him,
as it is stated: “He bears sin and passes over transgression.”
For whom does He bear sin?
For one who passes over transgression.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30 and supports רבא's teaching from step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: God ordered leniency in רב הונא's judgment because he was never exacting with others.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's teaching that one who is מעביר על מדותיו is forgiven
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's recovery

steps.title: Good news with a catch
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר חנינא looks at the end of the פסוק, 'לשארית נחלתו'. He calls it a fat tail with a thorn in it: the forgiveness is only for a remnant, not for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For the remnant of His inheritance.' רבי אחא בר חנינא said: This is a fat tail with a thorn in it. 'For the remnant of His inheritance' means not for all of His inheritance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the same פסוק. רבי אחא בר חנינא begins to explain them, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fat tail is a delicacy, but this one has a thorn in it. The good part is that God forgives. The 'thorn' is that the forgiveness is only for 'the remnant' of His people, not all of them. Who belongs to that remnant is explained in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: For the remnant of His inheritance
Fat tail of a sheep (a delicacy)

phrases.english: “For the remnant of His inheritance.”
Rabbi Aḥa bar Ḥanina said:
A fat tail with a thorn in it:
“For the remnant of His inheritance,” but not for all of His inheritance,
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״לִשְׁאֵרִית נַחֲלָתוֹ״, אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא: אַלְיָה וְקוֹץ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next words of the same פסוק in מיכה.
